# SPE Round r01 plan: triage agent

This is round 1. No `spe/` folder exists yet, so this plan creates it. I will make a local commit after each step. I will not push.

Defaults I chose where details were missing:
- I will build the agent in Python with the Anthropic SDK. It is one Messages API call per ticket with structured JSON output and no file tools.
- I will hold out 10 of the 40 tickets as a dev set, stratified by category. The other 30 are the test set. Prompts and few-shot examples come only from dev.
- I wrote the default thresholds for "correctly" and "cheaply" below. Each one is logged in `disagreements.md` for you to confirm.

## 1. Specify

Spec prompt (verbatim): "triage tickets correctly and cheaply."

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The output is valid JSON with `category`, `priority`, and `reply`. Category is one of billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. Priority is one of P1 to P4. | Project description | `check_schema` = 1.00 |
| R2 | Category matches the reference label on at least 85% of test tickets. | User: "correctly". Threshold is default D1 | `check_category` >= 0.85 |
| R3 | Priority matches exactly on at least 65% of test tickets and within one level on at least 90%. | User: "correctly". Thresholds are default D2 | `check_priority_exact` >= 0.65, `check_priority_near` >= 0.90 |
| R4 | No reference P1 ticket gets P3 or P4. | Decision D3. A missed outage costs the most. | `check_p1_floor` = 1.00 |
| R5 | The draft reply passes the judge rubric on at least 80% of test tickets. The rubric asks four things. Does it answer the customer's actual ask? Does it avoid invented facts? Does it give the right next step? Is it 150 words or fewer? | Project description: "drafts a first reply" | `judge_reply` >= 0.80 |
| R6 | The draft promises no refund, credit, or fix date. | Decision D4 | `check_no_promise` (regex) = 1.00, then judge confirms |
| R7 | Mean cost per ticket is at most $0.01 at current list price. | User: "cheaply". Threshold is default D5 | `usage_cost` <= 0.01 |
| R8 | The agent never sees test labels or test ticket text in its prompt. | SPE way | `check_leak` = pass, transcript scan |

### Disagreements and defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default chosen | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Category accuracy bar | 0.85 | You |
| D2 | Priority bars | 0.65 exact, 0.90 within one | You |
| D3 | P1 floor rule | No P1 labeled P3 or P4 | You |
| D4 | Promise ban in drafts | No refunds, credits, or dates | You, or the support lead |
| D5 | Cost bar | $0.01 per ticket | You |
| D6 | Data split | 10 dev, 30 test, stratified, fixed seed 7 | Logged default |
| D7 | Priority definitions | I write P1 to P4 definitions from the 10 dev tickets | Support lead should review before r02 |
| D8 | Judge model | Sonnet, a separate call that never sees the config name | Logged default |

## 2. Predict

Configurations. Each one changes one thing from C1.

| Config | What it is |
|---|---|
| C0 | Naive baseline. It always picks the majority dev category and P3, and sends a fixed template reply. No model call. |
| C1 | Sonnet, zero-shot, with category and priority definitions |
| C2 | C1 plus 5 few-shot examples from dev |
| C3 | C1 with Haiku in place of Sonnet |

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.03 | `check_schema` | Structured output makes JSON failures rare. The smaller model slips more often. |
| Category accuracy | 0.30 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | `check_category` | Most categories are clear from the text. Bug versus outage and account versus billing cause most errors. |
| Priority exact | 0.35 ± 0.10 | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.68 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_exact` | Priority follows the support lead's unwritten policy. Examples carry that policy better than definitions do. |
| Priority within one | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | `check_priority_near` | Most misses will be one level off. |
| P1 floor held | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.75 ± 0.25 | 0.75 ± 0.25 | 0.50 ± 0.25 | `check_p1_floor` | I expect about 4 P1 tickets in test, so each one moves the score by 0.25. Models tend to under-rate terse outage reports. |
| Reply judge pass | 0.00 ± 0.05 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.87 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | `judge_reply` | The template reply should fail every time. Sonnet writes good first replies. Haiku misses the actual ask more often. |
| No promise | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | `check_no_promise` | Models sometimes offer credits on billing tickets unless told not to. |
| Input tokens per ticket | 0 ± 0 | 1,200 ± 300 | 3,000 ± 600 | 1,200 ± 300 | `usage_tokens` | The system prompt is about 700 tokens and a ticket is about 400. Five examples add about 1,800. |
| Output tokens per ticket | 0 ± 0 | 350 ± 100 | 350 ± 100 | 380 ± 120 | `usage_tokens` | A 150-word reply plus JSON fields |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | 0 | filled at save | filled at save | filled at save | `usage_cost` | I will compute this from the token predictions using the current price list from the claude-api skill. I will not quote prices from memory. |

My headline prediction: C2 is the most accurate, C3 is the cheapest, and none of them meets R4 in round 1.

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps and gates

1. **Specify.** Create `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim. Create `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, and `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify`.
2. **Predict.** Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records the author as "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the bands, a Why for each number, and `same_as_last_round: n/a`. Commit `SPE r01 predict: C2 most accurate, C3 cheapest, P1 floor missed`. This happens before any harness work.
3. **Build.**
   - `triage/agent.py` holds the agent. Its prompt template lives in `triage/prompts/`.
   - `data/tickets_dev.jsonl` and `data/tickets_test.jsonl` hold ticket text only.
   - `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl` holds the reference labels. The agent code never imports or reads this path.
   - `spe/evals/graders/` holds the code checks and the judge prompt.
4. **Gate A: grader selftest.** The oracle (reference labels with a hand-written good reply) passes every code check. Empty output fails every check. Wrong labels (each category shifted by one) score 0 on `check_category`. The judge passes 3 good replies and fails 3 bad ones: an invented refund, an off-topic reply, and an empty reply. If any case fails, I stop and fix the grader.
5. **Gate B: control.** No earlier round exists, so I cannot regrade one. Instead, the grader score for C0 must equal a value I compute by hand from the label file.
6. **Gate C: dry run.** Run C1 and C3 on 2 dev tickets with 1 trial each. This confirms the pipeline runs end to end, tokens are logged, and cost is recorded.
7. **Gate D: leak check.** `check_leak` confirms that no rendered prompt contains test ticket text, test ticket IDs, or the `spe/evals/answers` path.
8. Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 1`. All prompt text gets the round number from that constant. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
9. **Launch the Workflow.** Each trial returns a schema: `ticket_id`, `config`, `trial`, `output`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost_usd`. Code checks run first. The judge runs only on `reply`, only after the code checks, and it never sees the config name.
10. **Split cells.** A cell is split when its trials disagree on category or priority. Each split cell gets up to 2 extra trials. Each config gets at most 30 extra trials.
11. **Peek scan.** The Workflow scans each trial transcript for reads of graders, answers, or predictions. It voids any trial that peeked and logs it.
12. **End of run.** A failure-analysis agent groups the errors into F-numbered types. A completeness critic checks that every cell in the prediction table has a measured value.
13. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
14. **Learn.** Write `spe/prediction-log.md`, including "Which Why broke". Write `spe/failures.md`. Add the "Proposed for round 2" table to the spec. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r01`.

### Workflow arguments

```
round: 1
configs: [C0, C1, C2, C3]
split: test (30 tickets)
trials_per_cell: 3
extra_trials_split_cell: 2
extra_trials_cap_per_config: 30
judge: sonnet, blind to config
cost_cap_usd: 15
on_cap: skip remaining trials, log skips, halt and report
```

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- Triage calls: 30 tickets × 3 trials × 3 model configs = 270. Up to 90 extra trials can be added. About 20 more calls come from the gates.
- Judge calls: about one per triage call, so up to about 380.
- Tokens: about 0.9M input and 0.15M output for triage. About 0.6M input and 0.08M output for judging.
- I expect the total to stay under $10. The hard cap is $15. I will check this against the current price list before launch.

### Halt conditions

I halt and report for any of these:
- The cost cap is hit.
- A grader selftest fails.
- A test label shows up in a prompt.
- A decision only you can make blocks the run, such as the D7 priority definitions turning out to conflict with the labels.

In all cases I make local commits only, with no push.
critiques: The plan quotes the spec verbatim ('triage tickets correctly and cheaply') and breaks it into R1 to R8. Each requirement has a source and a named test with a threshold, such as R2 'check_category >= 0.85' and R7 'usage_cost <= 0.01'.

The prediction table gives C0 to C3 numeric bands for every metric, such as category accuracy '0.85 ± 0.07' for C1 and '0.80 ± 0.08' for C3. One gap exists: the cost-per-ticket cells for C1 to C3 read 'filled at save'. The token rows those costs come from are numeric, so the table still meets the check.

The Why column gives one reason per metric row, not one per number. Several numbers have no stated reason. Examples are C0's category accuracy of 0.30, priority exact of 0.35, and within-one of 0.70. The cost cells also have only a method note. Under strict grading, this does not meet 'each predicted number'.

Step 2 copies the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and writes spe/predictions/r01.yaml with a 'Saved before the eval ran' header. It then commits 'SPE r01 predict' and says 'This happens before any harness work.'

The eval launches as a Workflow (step 9, r01-workflow.js). Gates come before it. Gate A is a grader selftest with oracle, empty, wrong-label, and judge cases. Gate C is a dry run of C1 and C3 on 2 dev tickets.
The prediction table has a 'Grader check' column. It ties each metric to a named check, such as check_schema, check_category, check_p1_floor, judge_reply, and usage_tokens or usage_cost.

Step 14 (Learn) writes spe/prediction-log.md, which includes 'Which Why broke'. It also writes failures.md, adds a 'Proposed for round 2' table, writes spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml, and tags spe-r01.
